H.domain: H = poly(n) for asymptotics; finite oracle is bounded

lambda.domain: lambda(n) must scale; 256 is only a finite reference

epsilon.domain: conditional on an explicitly stated computational assumption

P.domain: P >= 1; packing and metadata pages must be charged

s.scope: writer, independent readers, anchor, PIN registry, program-dependent advice

S.scope: data, roots, indexes, logs, generations and metadata

U_r.unit: complete remote page reads per SET

U_w.unit: complete remote page writes per SET
U_w.scope: data, root, metadata, WAL and amplification

U_delta.unit: changed logical data bits per SET
U_delta.scope: separate from page writes and no-op epoch change

Q_r.unit: complete remote page reads per range query

B_pi.unit: bytes sent as remote query proof and data
B_pi.scope: wire-format exact; separate from anchor traffic

C_author.unit: bytes of author to external services
C_author.scope: anchor publication, server requests, root and log pushes

C_reader.unit: bytes of reader to external services
C_reader.scope: server requests, remote data, catch-up and trusted-control requests

G.unit: prover primitive operations and bytes hashed

V.unit: verifier primitive operations and bytes hashed
V.scope: include local parity, hashing, and root comparison

A.scope: all SET publications and LATEST/PIN refresh reads

T.unit: setup and program bits, one-time I/O, preprocessed advice
T.scope: no state-dependent preprocessing free of charge

M.scope: pinned reachability, shared pages, index pages, root pages

GC_r.unit: complete remote pages read during collection

GC_w.unit: complete remote pages rewritten during collection

F.scope: record independently from operating-system page API calls

reader.latest_anchor_read: mandatory and charged for every freshness claim
reader.as_of_requires: prior trusted PIN token for that exact epoch

anchor.trust: separate ideal globally linearizable monotone epoch and authenticated root

pin_gc.pin_linearization: PIN_CURRENT must atomically register root before GC may reclaim that epoch
pin_gc.unpin_linearization: UNPIN permits reclamation only after authoritative revocation
pin_gc.races: serialize PIN, UNPIN, root admission and GC
pin_gc.retention: latest and every active pinned epoch
pin_gc.collector: no free global snapshot catalog or persistent pin database

soundness.bad_accept: reader accepts a wrong parity for trusted root/epoch
soundness.required: Pr[bad_accept] <= epsilon(lambda) under named binding assumptions

quantifiers.query: all nonempty intervals, including adaptive choices
quantifiers.history: arbitrary bounded sequence with two readers and PIN/UNPIN/GC
quantifiers.resource: worst-case and amortized costs stored separately; never infer worst-case from averages

model_separation.F1: malicious remote with separately charged trusted monotone anchor
model_separation.network: transport framing, retries and signatures excluded from reference but MUST be charged in full deployments
model_separation.remote_storage: fixed-stride page-image simulator; no free remote directory; all manifest and data bytes charged

forbidden_claims: first joint lower bound without full-text audit
constant hash digest is uniformly asymptotically secure
F0 Fenwick is an authenticated F1 protocol
PIN plus GC without atomic authority
an OS page API call is physical SSD write amplification
proof of real crash safety from ideal fsync

remote_manifest_format.fixed_region: manifest and data separately page aligned

reference_storage_layout.remote_locator: public arithmetic fixed stride; no state-dependent remote epoch-to-object directory or free B-tree
reference_storage_layout.remote_simulator: in-memory dictionaries represent content at deterministic physical slot addresses; keys are not a free oracle for read/GC
reference_storage_layout.gc_enumeration: probe every issued epoch slot 0..H, including holes; count at least manifest pages per attempted remote lookup

pin_registry.format: one-byte reader ID plus eight-byte epoch plus 32-byte digest
pin_registry.persistent_authority_page_writes: ceil(41/P) per PIN/UNPIN, separate from remote S and U_w

limitations: Sparse page holes are abstractly reclaimed, not real filesystem punches
Atomic trust anchor and PIN authority are idealized and separately charged
Catalog scanning counts page API probes including missing slots; concrete filesystem API not implemented
No cryptographic reduction or source physical durability proof
